absorbed.basis: direct — grounding brief §3 finding 1 (343-card/#222 stale-mirror incident, sdlc-schema.json re-vendoring pattern) has no hand-authored who-declares-dependence record anywhere today.
direct — same grounding brief §3 finding 1; a hand-authored manifest alone cannot be trusted to stay current, so consumption facts should be self-reported by the vendoring gates at run time.
external — a schema diff alone says nothing about which consumers are actually exposed vs. merely adjacent; this facet ranks exposure severity rather than producing a flat unranked consumer list.

executor_profile.justification: Matches the issue-map's own executor recommendation. Three coordinated CLI/data scripts (manifest reader, self-registration writer, ranking script) sharing one consumer-index module against an already-understood existing gate (check_issue_contract_parity.py) — mechanical scaffolding, not open-ended architectural judgment; all three views share one file/data boundary and do not require cross-subsystem reviewer consensus.

mutation_summary.detail: Record created issue on draft and sidecar

source_artifact.content_excerpt: Who-consumes-X is one dataset with three views: the hand-authored manifest with change-time checklists, gates self-registering their copies centrally, and field-level exposure ranking on a schema diff.
